title: Knowing When to Abstain: Medical LLMs Under Clinical Uncertainty

paper.authors: Machcha, Yerra, Gupta, Sahoo, Sultana, Yu, Yao (UMass Amherst / VA Bedford / UMass Lowell)

dependence.note: The benchmark measures the LLMs' own answer probabilities (top-logprobs) to derive conformal set sizes and abstention rates; every reported number is a property of model outputs.

claim.statement: On MedQA (1,007 test items; 30% calibration / 70% test; alpha = 0.1; temperature 0; single-token answer with top-logprobs), gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 never selects the explicit abstention option (abstention rate 0.0000 in every A/AP variant, zero- and few-shot, CoT and no-CoT), while its accuracy falls from 0.5404 (NA, zero-shot, no-CoT) to 0.4099 with the abstention option and 0.3688 with abstention + perturbation, and its LAC set size grows 3.80 -> 4.21 -> 4.51 (Table 6); under the CoT prompt its accuracy collapses to ~0.25 with set size equal to all options (5.0 / 6.0) (Table 5).
claim.metric: accuracy (argmax over option logprobs); conformal-prediction set size (LAC and APS) at alpha = 0.1; abstention rate = share of test items whose argmax is the abstention option
claim.original_source: Appendix Table 6 (MedQA, no chain-of-thought) and Table 5 (MedQA, chain-of-thought); Appendix E model list; Section 4.3 setup; 'The MedQA dataset included 1007 test examples' (Appendix)

protocol.model_note: Explicit in Appendix E (closed-source: gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14, gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18, gpt-4o-2024-08-06, gpt-4.1-2025-04-14); o4 excluded because no logprobs
protocol.prompt_source: quantify_uncertainty/prompts/prompt_templates.py - shared_zero_prompt ('The following is a multiple-choice question with {num_choices} potential answers. Only one of these options is correct. Please make your best effort and select the correct answer. You only need to output the option.') and shared_cot_prompt ('... Please reason step-by-step and select the correct answer. You only need to output the option.'); formatting in prompt_helpers.py ('Question: ... Choices: A. ... Answer:'); paper Appendix G

params.seed: not set (calibration/test split is an unseeded random 30/70 stratified split)
params.other: single user message; few-shot k = 4 dynamic examples via text-embedding-ada-002 kNN from the train pool; perturbed variants pre-generated with gpt-4.1-mini; abstention option string 'I am unable to answer this question for certain reasons.' inserted at a random position; missing options in top_logprobs imputed at (min logprob - 5)

protocol.n_items_note: per dataset variant (NA, A, NAP, AP), each under zero-shot / few-shot and CoT / no-CoT
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: accuracy = argmax option vs gold; LAC/APS conformal sets from the 30% calibration split (quantify_uncertainty/metrics/cp_sets.py, cp_metrics.py; alpha = 0.1); abstention rate; run via scripts_closed_models/python/launch_experiment.py -> evaluate_outputs_with_conformal()

calibration/test split is an unseeded random 30/70 split, so conformal set sizes vary run to run

protocol artifact: max_tokens = 1 combined with the 'reason step-by-step' CoT prompt means the first emitted token is not an option letter - the CoT-condition numbers (accuracy ~0.25, set size = all options) measure the artifact, not capability
missing options in top_logprobs are imputed at (min - 5) logprob, which shapes the set sizes

budget.assumptions: Core grid = 4 variants x zero-shot x {no-CoT, CoT} = 8 x 1,007 items x 3 seeds; ~450 input tokens, 1 output token. Adding the few-shot conditions (k = 4, ~2,000 input tokens) costs ~USD 4.8 more (full MedQA grid ~USD 6).

user_checks: Core claim: the gpt-4.1-nano Table 6 row as drafted, or the paper-level claim 'adding an abstention option raises uncertainty more than perturbation' aggregated across models?
Include the CoT condition in the re-run (reproduces the max_tokens = 1 artifact) or exclude it as an identified protocol flaw?
Fix a calibration-split seed and report over multiple splits (repo uses an unseeded random split)?
domain_notes: MedQA (USMLE) 4-5-option questions plus an inserted abstention option; in the perturbed abstention variants 25% of items have the abstention option as the gold answer, so abstaining can be correct. Conformal set sizes are only meaningful relative to the number of options (5 or 6): gpt-4.1-nano's 3.8-4.5 indicates nearly uninformative option probabilities, and 0% abstention means the model never ranks the abstention option first even when information is missing. The paper's broader claim (abstention option > perturbation as an uncertainty driver; scale and CoT help little) is a cross-model aggregate, of which this card tests one live-model slice.
